title: Best 70-Pint Dehumidifier (2026): Genuine 70-Pint Picks
h1: The Best 70-Pint Dehumidifiers (That Really Are 70 Pints)
dek: Since the 2019 test change, plenty of “70-pint” boxes hold 50-pint machines. These picks are rated for the real thing.
description: The best 70 pint dehumidifier for 2026 — GE, Honeywell, Frigidaire and Ivation compared on DOE 2019 capacity, pumps, Wi-Fi and the naming traps to avoid.
intro: A **70-pint dehumidifier** is the biggest portable size most homes will ever need — the one for a damp basement, a musty utility room or a space that floods a little every spring. The trouble is that the label doesn’t always mean what it used to.

In 2019 the Department of Energy changed its test conditions from 80°F to a cooler 65°F, which produces lower numbers for the same machine. Many former “70-pint” units are now rated at 50 pints, and some still carry a 70 in their name or marketing. We only included models listed at 70 pints under the current standard, so you’re not paying for capacity you won’t get.
Here are the best picks, from a self-draining model for basements without a floor drain to a Wi-Fi unit you can check from your phone.
topPicksLead: The **GE APEH70LW** is the best 70-pint dehumidifier for most basements, because its built-in pump can push water up and out without a floor drain.

blocks.text: That middle number surprises people. A 70-pint unit doesn’t necessarily cover a bigger room than a 50-pint one; it pulls water out faster in a space that’s actively damp. Some retailers even list former 70-pint models as “50 pint (previously 70 pint).”

We don’t lab-test dehumidifiers. We started from DOE 2019 capacity ratings and ENERGY STAR listings, then checked manufacturer spec sheets and manuals for drainage, low-temperature operation and features. We cross-referenced CPSC recall records and read owner reviews for recurring problems such as failing pumps, icing coils and leaking buckets.
We excluded units whose “70-pint” label reflects the old test, and gave extra weight to drainage options, since a 70-pint machine in a damp basement can fill a bucket several times a day.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 70-pint dehumidifier

items.label: The DOE 2019 rating
items.text: Check the spec sheet or EnergyGuide label, not the model name. A 70 in the name doesn’t guarantee 70 pints today.

items.label: A drainage plan
items.text: No floor drain nearby? Choose a pump model. Have one? A gravity hose saves money. Our [drain hose picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-drain-hose/) cover the options.

items.label: Real need for the capacity
items.text: If your space is merely damp rather than wet, a [50-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-50-pint-dehumidifier/) may be all you need.

items.label: Cold-basement performance
items.text: Below about 65°F, compressor units lose capacity and can ice up. Look for auto-defrost if your basement is chilly.

items.label: Mobility
items.text: These units are heavy. Casters and solid handles matter if you’ll move it.

blocks.title: Buying an older 70-pint unit?
blocks.text: Check the model and manufacture date against CPSC recalls before you buy secondhand. Several 70-pint models sold between 2009 and 2017 were part of the 2021 New Widetech fire-hazard recall.

sections.heading: Getting the most from a 70-pint dehumidifier

items: Set the humidistat to 45–50% rather than running it on continuous — it will cycle off once the space is dry and save energy.
Keep it at least a foot from walls and furniture so air can reach the intake and exhaust freely.
Close basement windows and doors to the outside while it runs; otherwise you’re drying the neighborhood.
Clean the filter every couple of weeks during heavy use. A clogged filter cuts airflow and capacity.
In a cool basement, watch for frost on the coils and raise the room temperature or use defrost mode if it appears.

blocks.text: A big unit running much of the summer adds noticeably to your power bill. Our guide to [how much electricity a dehumidifier uses](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) shows how to estimate the cost, and ENERGY STAR models keep it down.

The **GE APEH70LW** is the best 70-pint dehumidifier for most basements thanks to its built-in pump. Choose the **Honeywell TP70WK** to save money if you have a floor drain, the **Frigidaire FGAC7044U1** for app control, and the **Ivation IVALDH70PW** if you’ll roll it between spaces. Always confirm the DOE 2019 rating — and if even 70 pints isn’t enough, look at a [whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/).

faqs.a: The GE APEH70LW for most homes. It has a built-in pump with a 16-foot lift, so it drains without a floor drain. The Honeywell TP70WK is the budget pick and the Frigidaire FGAC7044U1 adds Wi-Fi.

faqs.q: Is a 70-pint dehumidifier the same as it used to be?
faqs.a: Not always. The 2019 DOE test runs at 65°F instead of 80°F, so many older “70-pint” models are now rated at 50 pints. Check for a DOE 2019 rating on the spec sheet or EnergyGuide label.

faqs.q: Is the Frigidaire 70-pint dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: The FGAC7044U1 is a good choice if you want app and Alexa control with genuine 70-pint capacity. If you need hands-free drainage without a floor drain, a pump model like the GE APEH70LW is more convenient.

faqs.q: What’s the difference between the Honeywell TP70WK and TP70PWKN?
faqs.a: Despite the shared “70,” the TP70PWKN is a 50-pint (DOE 2019) unit with a pump, while the TP70WK is listed as Honeywell’s 70-pint model without one. Always check the rated capacity, not the name.

faqs.q: Is the Aprilaire E070 a 70-pint dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Yes — it removes 70 pints a day, but it’s a permanently installed, bucketless unit for sealed crawl spaces rather than a portable. See our [Aprilaire guide](/best/best-aprilaire-dehumidifier/) for details.

faqs.q: What size space does a 70-pint dehumidifier cover?
faqs.a: Most are listed for up to about 4,500 sq ft, similar to many 50-pint models. The extra capacity removes moisture faster in a very damp space rather than covering a much bigger area. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) helps you decide.
